items.q: What does Pana say is wrong with 5×5 and progressive overload?
items.a: **Nothing inherent.** They are still the **base**. They fail at a **real strength plateau** — then you need unusual placement of heavies, not a new religion.

items.q: What is the one concept most people miss about getting stronger?
items.a: **Strength is a skill**, like guitar or football. Genetic freaks skip the practice; he was a **skinny intermediate**. Practice the **heavy single** you actually miss.

items.q: How did he program two squat singles in a week?
items.a: Tuesday **86–89%** 1RM, Saturday **89–94%**, then **raise the percents** across the cycle. **Practice singles, not max-outs.** Still do volume, technique, accessories — do not stack a **5×5 plus a single** the same day without thinning the week.

items.q: What stall did this break, and why was he missing in meets?
items.a: Squat stuck ~**230 kg** for months. He avoided heavy singles in training, then got **nervous** on the platform and **technique collapsed**. More submaximal singles = **exposure** (like a growing speaking audience) plus CNS/technique work. Result he cites: **230 → 250 kg**.

items.q: What numbers does he use to kill 'you must bulk to get strong'?
items.a: Bench **120 kg at 74 kg** body weight vs **178 kg at 65.7 kg**. Total **500 kg at 74 kg** vs **713 kg at ~66 kg** (~**7–8%** body fat, more muscle). Years apart, not six months — still a cut, not a bulk.

items.q: What three rules keep strength alive in a deficit?
items.a: **100–200 kcal** deficit, not 500–700 (crash cuts dump muscle). **Gain muscle while losing fat.** Stack ~**70% of carbs** around training: **40–50% ~2 h before**, **20–30% after**. Skip this if you are already lean.

items.q: What is his actual potentiation protocol, vs the 150% walkout meme?
items.a: Not unracking **150%** so 100% 'feels light.' Before **3×5 at 78%**, hit **~87–88% × 1**, then the volume. CNS primed → later sets **more explosive** and psychologically lighter. **Bench > squat > deadlift**; pulls maybe **85–86%**.

items.q: Should you run extra heavies all year?
items.a: Only if you **recover extremely well**. Otherwise **8–10 weeks on**, **8–10 weeks off**, especially into a meet. Same caution: extra heavies **fatigue joints and low back**.
